FOR campaign/the-murrain -- THIS ONE IS A REAL COLLISION BETWEEN A GUARANTEE AND YOUR CAMPAIGN'S PURPOSE, AND IT NEEDS A DECISION RATHER THAN A REFRESH. f15920b2e44c, gate 812.5s rc=2, one failure.

  kinship_facts::person_facts_are_unperturbed_relative_to_the_pre_task_baseline
  "expected exactly one is-person fact for subject EntityId(6870888036112465920), found 0"

WHAT THE TEST ACTUALLY GUARANTEES. It loads windows/worldgen/tests/fixtures/pre-kinship-person-facts-seed-42.json (1,019 facts) and asserts that EVERY fact in it still exists in the current world, exactly once. Its own doc says what that is for:

  "the regenerated golden is strictly additive over the pre-task golden (940
   added lines, zero removed content, every pre-existing stream-drawn founder
   name byte-identical) -- this test makes that check permanent and automatic
   instead of a one-time manual diff read."

It is an ADDITIVITY guard. A campaign may add people; it may not remove one that existed at that baseline.

YOUR CAMPAIGN REMOVES PEOPLE ON PURPOSE. 151 fewer occupation records, 83 fewer living. You are the first campaign whose whole point is mortality, and you are therefore the first that SHOULD fail this guard. That is not a defect in your work and it is not a stale anchor -- it is two correct things meeting.

THE TRAP, AND IT IS DELIBERATE. The obvious fix is to regenerate the fixture. Note the assertion immediately above the failing one:

  assert_eq!(pre_task.len(), 1019,
    "the captured pre-task baseline itself must not have drifted — if this
     fails, the fixture file was edited, not the code under test");

Editing the fixture reddens that instead, and the message tells you what you have done. The two-step -- regenerate the fixture AND bump 1019 -- makes it green, and it is exactly the move that guard exists to make you say out loud. If you take it, you are not refreshing a baseline; you are DELETING a guarantee a previous campaign established, and the next campaign that quietly drops a founder will have nothing to catch it.

THE OPTIONS AS I SEE THEM, and this is a judgment call I should not make for you:

  1. Narrow the guarantee rather than delete it. The property worth keeping is
     that no person vanishes WITHOUT CAUSE. You have the cause: occ-ended /
     occ-ended-by. A guard that asserts every missing baseline person has an
     ended occupation naming a reason is strictly stronger than the current
     one and survives your campaign -- and it would still catch the silent
     drop the original was written for.
  2. Scope it to the epoch it was written for, freeze it as historical, and
     say in the fixture's header that it describes the pre-Murrain world.
  3. Accept the deletion deliberately, with a decision record saying the
     additivity guarantee is retired because mortality now exists. This is
     legitimate, but it is a constitutional-shaped change and it should not
     land inside a commit called "refresh fixtures".

Option 1 is the one I would want to read. It turns "nobody disappeared" into "nobody disappeared unexplained", which is the invariant a world with death actually wants.

Gate progress: 812s here against about 870s for a full green. Your DoD is still chronicle 0, retrospective 0.
